findings.message: tasks.md task 3.3 removes `languageResolutionOptions` and `localeResources` from `src/i18n.ts` (it keeps temporary re-exports only for `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE`, `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` and the language type), but `packages/client/src/test/setup.ts:5` imports `{ languageResolutionOptions, localeResources } from "@/i18n"` and uses them in the global i18next init (lines 33-39: `resources: localeResources, ...languageResolutionOptions, lng: "ru", fallbackLng: "ru"`). This setup file runs for every Vitest test, so after task 3.3 every jsdom test runs with no translation resources and typecheck fails. No task updates test/setup.ts, for example to build its options with `createI18nOptions(localeRegistry)` and `lng: "ru"`, and task 4.4's list of importers to move from `@/i18n` does not name it. Add this step to task 3.3 (or a task right after it) with a verifying test run, and mention it in design D8 under 'Existing tests that the change touches'.

findings.message: Planned behaviour silently breaks the existing jsdom suites and no task handles it: test/setup.ts initializes i18next with lng 'ru', and dozens of jsdom tests switch the language with i18n.changeLanguage('ru') before rendering AppShell (AppShell.test.tsx, AppShell.settings.test.tsx, settingsWorld.tsx, hourFormatWorld.tsx, many unit BDD worlds). Design D3 adds useInterfaceLanguage() to AppShellContent, which resolves resolveInterfaceLanguage(preferences.interfaceLanguage /* null */, readBrowserLanguages()) and calls i18n.changeLanguage in a useLayoutEffect when it differs. jsdom's navigator.languages is ['en-US'], so every rendered AppShell switches to 'en'. No task stubs readBrowserLanguages / navigator.languages in test/setup.ts or otherwise keeps today's Russian default, and design D8 wrongly claims the setup 'keeps the lng: "ru" … overrides' and so today's behaviour. Task 7.3's verification (`npx vitest run src/app`) and 11.2 (`pnpm --filter @time-zones/client test`) would fail. Add a task (and design note) that pins the browser languages for jsdom tests, e.g. stubbing readBrowserLanguages to ['ru'] in test/setup.ts, and check the AppShell-rendering suites.

Task order is not followable: task 3.3 removes `SupportedLanguage` from i18n.ts and only re-exports `InterfaceLanguageCode`, yet ~20 modules still `import type { SupportedLanguage } from "@/i18n"` (ports/citySearch.ts, adapters/city-search/*, presenter/*, controller/use*.ts, constants/date.ts, test steps). The registry-derived SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES also becomes string[], so zoneCitiesSource.ts indexing `names: { en; ru }` and `FIRST_DAY_OF_WEEK_BY_LANGUAGE: Record<SupportedLanguage, number>` stop typechecking. Those are only fixed in tasks 4.2–4.4, so 3.3's own verification `pnpm --filter @time-zones/client typecheck` cannot pass. Either keep a `SupportedLanguage` alias re-export (and the old literal types) until task 4, or move the typecheck verification to task 4.4.

Minor (code-style.md: 'Is any value repeated in 2+ places? → Must be a constant'): task 10.1 keeps seedLanguage in locations_ui_e2e.fixtures.ts using its local `const LANGUAGE_STORAGE_KEY = "language"` while task 6.2 introduces `LEGACY_STORAGE_KEYS.LANGUAGE`. The task should switch the seed to the new constant.

findings.message: tasks.md does not deliver success metric M6. proposal.md M6 says: "Stryker scores at least 95 % (minimum acceptable 90 %) on every new or changed production file of this change." Task 11.1 runs scoped Stryker on only 20 files. It leaves out production files the change edits: adapters/locationsDocument.ts (task 6.1), preferences/preferences.ts (5.2), adapters/city-search/zoneCitiesSource.ts and createCompositeCitySearch.ts (4.2), the six hooks useCitySearch, useWallTimeInput, useExemplarCity, useReferenceMoment, useCalendarMonth and useLocations, plus useDocumentLanguage (4.4), app/AppShell.tsx (7.3) and locales/index.ts (2.8). Either add scoped runs (at most 5 files each) for these files, or narrow M6 to the listed new files.

specs/app-shell/spec.md, scenario "Registry from locale files": "THEN it lists `de`, `en` and `ru`, sorted by `name`". Sorting by name (English, German, Russian) gives en, de, ru, and task 2.3 expects "codes `en`, `de`, `ru`, sorted by `name`". The spec lists them in code order, so the Gherkin step of task 2.8 could assert either order. Write the scenario's list in name order: `en`, `de`, `ru`.

NFR-P1 (proposal: "After a language change, presenting 50 rows builds at most one formatter per time zone and label kind in use") has no requirement in the spec deltas. The existing settings requirement "Preferences are fast" (openspec/specs/settings/spec.md:247) holds the same kind of bound for the hour format, but the delta neither modifies it nor adds a language scenario. Task 9.1 still creates the Gherkin scenarios "Presenting again with the same language builds no formatter" and "Switching the language builds one formatter per zone and kind", which then have no spec behind them. Add a MODIFIED "Preferences are fast" with these scenarios, and list it under Capabilities in the proposal.
